title: sparse-page-rebalancer-and-slab-morphing-spec
content:
Overview

This doc proposes the "sparse page rebalancer" and a complementary "slab morphing" mechanism to reduce long-tail fragmentation in the KV cache while preserving low tail latency for token generation workloads. The design targets production constraints: sub-ms hot-path, low interference with inference kernels, and bounded background compaction cost under high throughput.

Motivation and problem statement

We observe three classes of fragmentation that degrade steady-state memory efficiency:
1) micro-holes created by variable-length entries when stored inside fixed-size pages;
2) skewed occupancy across per-shard arenas (hot shards densely packed, cold shards sparse);
3) long-lived small entries that prevent coalescing and force large page retention. Existing LRU/approx-LRU eviction leaves fragmented free space that is unusable without expensive stop-the-world compaction.

Goals
- Recover usable capacity by compacting/reshaping pages incrementally without violating latency SLOs.
- Avoid global stop-the-world passes; make compaction preemptible and schedulable.
- Provide operational knobs for aggressiveness and cost budget.
- Keep serving runtime kernel fast-path unchanged for hits; background processes should be off-main-path.

Terminology
- page: unit of allocation backed by GPU/host memory (typical sizes: 64KB, 1MB variants).
- micro-slot: variable-length record region inside a page.
- slab bin: fixed-size allocator bucket for same-sized objects (powers of two).
- hole-score: heuristic indicating fragmentation inside a page (0..1).
- rebalancer: background component that compacts pages by moving live micro-slots to reduce holes and free pages.
- morphing: operation that merges/splits slab bins to better match workload size distribution.

Design overview

1) Multi-granularity page layout
- Each arena maintains a mix of page types: slab pages (homogeneous object sizes), packed pages (many variable-length micro-slots for chat KV), and sparse pages (lightly used pages held for rebalancing).
- New allocations prefer slab pages if object size <= slab_max_small (e.g., 1KB). Otherwise packed pages are used.
- Pages include a small header with an occupancy bitmap and a compact free-list; header size kept < 64 bytes to avoid cacheline explosions.

2) Hole-score and page candidacy
- hole-score = (free_bytes + fragmentation_penalty) / page_capacity. fragmentation_penalty is proportional to number of free fragments > 2 and small contiguous runs < min_coalesce.
- Pages with hole-score >= reclaim_threshold (default 0.45) are candidate for rebalancer.

3) Rebalancer algorithm (background, per-arena)
- Runs as a set of cooperative tasks attached to the runtime scheduler with a budget measured in CPU ms and GPU copy bandwidth per second.
- Candidate selection: pick the top-N pages by hole-score within shard/arena, but cap N by budget to avoid IO storms.
- For each page P:
  - Allocate a target page T from either slab or packed pool depending on live-object size distribution sampled from P. Allocation should try to co-locate with hot-access shard to reduce cross-device transfers.
  - Move live micro-slots from P -> T via copy operations that leverage bulk memcpy kernels. For GPU-backed pages, use asynchronous device-to-device or device-to-host-device copies with stream priority low.
  - Update indirections atomically by writing a few-word forwarding entry: the runtime keeps a small epoch/forwarding table per key to make in-flight accesses forward to the new location.
  - When moved objects fall below a compaction-success threshold (e.g., >60% bytes moved off P), mark P recyclable and return to free pool; otherwise postpone further work on P.

4) Slab morphing (adaptive bin resizing)
- Continuously sample allocation histogram per-arena. Maintain N slab bins (power-of-two sizes) but allow runtime to create ephemeral split/merged bins: e.g., merge two adjacent small bins into a larger bin when the small bins are underutilized and fragmentation across them exceeds a threshold.
- Morphing operations are lightweight: they mark a bin as transitioning, divert new allocations to a shadow bin, and gradually relocate live objects using the same rebalancer pipeline.
- Example: if 4KB bin usage < 20% and aggregated holes > 35%, merge with 8KB bin to reduce inter-bin fragmentation for mid-sized allocations.

5) Eviction policy integration
- Eviction remains LRU-approx for steady-state but is augmented with a fragmentation-aware eviction hint: when choosing a victim set, prefer evicting objects whose eviction would create large contiguous free runs on a page (benefit score = expected free-run increase / token-cost).
- When eviction candidates are insufficient, trigger a higher-priority rebalancer pass scoped to the affected arena.

6) Scheduling, cost controls, and kernel considerations
- Rebalancer tasks are scheduled with three adjustable budgets: CPU_ms_per_sec, GPU_copy_bytes_per_sec, and max_concurrent_pages. Defaults tuned to 2% CPU, 5% device memcpy bandwidth.
- Compaction uses low-priority CUDA streams (or corresponding async DMA) to avoid interfering with inference kernels. If device load exceeds a threshold (e.g., kernel-miss-ratio), rebalancer backs off exponentially.
- For NUMA/enclave setups, rebalancer honors placement: do not move pages across NUMA nodes unless cross-node benefit exceeds cost (measured by expected eviction reduction).

7) Observability and metrics
- Per-arena metrics: hole_score_histogram, pages_reclaimed/sec, bytes_compacted/sec, compaction_latency_p50/p95, rebalancer_backoff_events, slab_morph_events.
- Tracing points: page_candidate_selected, copy_started(copy_id, size, src_page, dst_page), forward_entry_published, page_released.

8) Safety and correctness
- Forwarding table: small atomic pointer indirections kept in fast path for in-flight lookups; worst-case extra indirection adds one pointer chase.
- Rebalancer must preserve consistency with concurrent readers/writers: writers that append to a source page acquire a lightweight ephemeral write token that prevents relocation of a micro-slot currently being updated.
- Crash recovery: on startup the runtime scans forwarding table entries and completes or rolls back partially moved objects using a idempotent move log. The log is ring-buffered and persisted to volatile NVRAM only when required by Private deployments.

9) Simulation and rollout plan
- Implement an in-memory simulator that consumes production trace samples: track allocation patterns, simulate rebalancer with different budgets and policies, and measure effective capacity gains and additional CPU/GPU cost.
- Canary rollout: enable rebalancer in read-only observation mode on a subset of dedicated clusters for 2 weeks, then enable low-aggressiveness compaction, monitor compaction latency and inference tail latency. Gradually increase aggressiveness if metrics safe.

10) Experiments to validate
- Microbench: synthetic workloads with small-churn chat KV and large static embeddings to observe morphing thresholds.
- Cost experiment: measure increase in memcpy bandwidth and CPU vs reclaimed bytes to compute reclaim efficiency (bytes reclaimed / CPU_ms).
- Failure injection: force rebalancer preemption and partial copy to validate forwarding table correctness and recovery logic.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How to pick page size mix for mixed-host/GPU memory to maximize DMA efficiency?
- Forwarding indirections increase lookup cost; quantify p99 impact and whether additional hardware-accelerated indirections (e.g., small per-key cache) are warranted.
- Is it worth integrating eviction hints directly into the admission path for generation tokens when near capacity?

Operational knobs (initial proposed defaults)
- reclaim_threshold: 0.45
- compaction_budget_cpu_ms_per_sec: 20
- compaction_budget_gpu_bytes_per_sec: 40MB/s per device
- max_concurrent_pages_per_arena: 4
- slab_morph_check_interval_sec: 300

Next steps
- Build in-memory simulator (owner: Daniel Kim) and run against 30 days of sampled production traces.
- Prototype forwarding table and async copy pipeline in a feature branch (owner: Priya Shah).
- Draft observability dashboard and alert rules for compaction regressions (owner: Ava Martinez).

Appendix: compact move pseudo-code

for page in pick_candidates(arena, budget):
  dst = allocate_target_page(arena, sample_layout(page))
  for obj in live_objects(page):
    if try_acquire_move_token(obj):
      async_copy(obj.src_addr, dst.next_free, callback=publish_forwarding(obj.key, dst.addr))
    else:
      skip
  wait_for_completion_or_budget()
  if moved_bytes(page) >= page.capacity * reclaim_success_fraction:
    mark_page_free(page)
  else:
    postpone(page)
